full_caption: Nikolai Kettleburn, Appellant, v. Applegate Commons Property Group, Inc., Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Nikolai Kettleburn claims title by adverse possession to a 24.0-acre wooded tract adjoining 4166 Mill Race Way, Pinecrest, SB, of which Applegate Commons Property Group, Inc. is the record owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The trial court found the elements satisfied as to 22.6 acres and not satisfied as to the remainder, which lay beyond any fence or posted line. That allocation is not clearly erroneous.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Nikolai Kettleburn posted the tract against trespass in 2002, cut and sold standing timber in 2013 and 2025, and maintained a hunting camp on the northeast quarter continuously thereafter.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Land held by a municipality for a public purpose is not subject to adverse possession. The 50-foot strip within the platted right of way is therefore excluded from any judgment in Nikolai Kettleburn's favor.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Continuity is broken by an entry of the record owner made with intent to reclaim possession. The single survey visit by Applegate Commons Property Group, Inc.'s agent in 2035, unaccompanied by any assertion of possession, did not interrupt the running of the statute.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Color of title is not required where the claim rests on actual occupancy, but it enlarges the claim to the full extent of the described premises rather than the portion actually occupied.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Possession is 'actual' where the claimant uses the land as an ordinary owner of similar land would use it. For wooded acreage, selective timbering, posting, and seasonal recreational use may suffice where cultivation would not be expected.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Hostility does not require ill will. It requires only that the possession be without the record owner's permission and inconsistent with the owner's title. A claimant's mistaken belief as to the true line does not defeat hostility in this State.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Affirmed in part, reversed in part, and remanded for entry of a decree describing the vested tract by metes and bounds consistent with the surveyor's Exhibit A.

sections.heading: RIDER 1 — STATEMENT OF CLAIM AND DESCRIPTION
sections.text: Claimant asserts title by adverse possession to a tract of 24.0 acres more particularly described in the surveyor's Exhibit A, being that portion of the record parcel lying east of the posted line and north of the old rail grade, and claims the same in fee simple absolute as against all persons.

sections.heading: RIDER 5 — QUIET TITLE RELIEF REQUESTED
sections.text: Claimant requests a decree quieting title in Claimant as against Respondent and all persons claiming under Respondent, describing the vested tract by metes and bounds, directing the Recorder to index the decree against both parcels, and awarding costs. Claimant does not seek damages for the period of possession.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Severability
sections.text: If any provision of this instrument is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to render it enforceable, and if it cannot be so reformed it shall be severed, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Force Majeure
sections.text: Neither party shall be liable for a failure of performance, other than an obligation to pay money, caused by an act of God, flood, fire, civil disturbance, governmental order, epidemic, or other cause beyond that party's reasonable control, provided the affected party gives notice within 7 days and resumes performance as promptly as practicable.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Governing Law
sections.text: This instrument shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Sable, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Any action arising out of or relating to this instrument shall be brought exclusively in the courts sitting in Pinecrest County, Sable, and each party consents to the personal jurisdiction of those courts.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Recording
sections.text: This instrument shall be recorded in the land records of Pinecrest County, Sable, and shall run with the land, binding upon and inuring to the benefit of the parties and their respective heirs, successors, personal representatives and assigns. The party causing the instrument to be recorded shall bear the recording fees and shall furnish a conformed copy to the other party within 7 days of recording.
